operation: Open "D:/mimic-iv-3.1/hosp.duckdb" read-only (DuckDB ATTACH ... READ_ONLY), copy the table final_cohort_patient_level unchanged with SELECT * to Parquet, and write nothing to the DuckDB file.

Verify 9902 rows and 146 columns, that subject_id and stay_id are nonmissing and unique (first qualifying septic ICU stay per patient) and that hadm_id is nonmissing. Write one row per column (dtype, missing count) and per identifier check, and stop if an identifier check fails.

analysis_method: Exposure, outcome and time-variable consistency check
operation: Count violations of: pravastatin_exposed in {0,1} and equal to exposure_status=='pravastatin'; no excluded_other_statin rows; exposed rows have 0<=hours_to_first_pravastatin<=48 and unexposed rows have no pravastatin time; age>=18; death_28d, discharged_alive_before_28d in {0,1} and not both 1; event_status coded 1/2/0; 0<=followup_days<=28 with 28 for event_status 0; followup_end_time>=intime. Stop if any rule fails.

Tabulate each study-design element against available columns and against the approach of published MIMIC-IV statin-sepsis cohorts (Front Immunol 2025 doi:10.3389/fimmu.2025.1537172; Front Pharmacol 2025 doi:10.3389/fphar.2025.1610450 and doi:10.3389/fphar.2025.1520107; Front Neurol 2024 doi:10.3389/fneur.2024.1371314). Record: primary outcome is 28-day all-cause mortality from ICU admission using deathtime or dod (post-discharge deaths included, as in the published studies) instead of in-hospital death censored at discharge, which is kept as a design-specified secondary analysis; the primary analysis is 1:1 nearest-neighbour propensity-score matching (caliper 0.05 on the propensity-score scale, without replacement) followed by Cox regression in the matched cohort, with stabilized IPTW, overlap weighting and multivariable Cox models as sensitivity analyses; SAPS II, APS III and LODS are not available so SOFA is used; mechanical ventilation and RRT are not adjusted for because the design treats them as post-exposure; exposure within 48 h follows the published early-statin (48 h) design, and immortal time is examined with a 48-hour landmark and a time-dependent exposure Cox model.

Write a JSON specification. Exposure: pravastatin_exposed. Primary outcome: time28_all/death28_all (28-day all-cause death from intime using deathtime, else dod at 12:00, complete follow-up to day 28). Secondary outcomes: time90_all/death90_all, hosp_death (hospital_expire_flag), icu_death (deathtime <= outtime + 6 h), icu_los_days (los), hosp_los_days; design-specified outcome followup_days/death_28d/event_status. PS covariates: continuous age, charlson_index, sofa_total_24h, hours_admit_to_icu, weight_kg, heart_rate_max, mbp_min, resp_rate_max, temperature_max, spo2_min, gcs_min, lactate_max, creatinine_max, platelets_min, wbc_max, hemoglobin_min, bicarbonate_min, bun_max, glucose_max, urine_output_24h_ml; binary female, cm_myocardial_infarction, cm_congestive_heart_failure, cm_peripheral_vascular, cm_cerebrovascular, cm_chronic_pulmonary, cm_renal, cm_malignancy, cm_metastatic_tumor, cm_severe_liver, cm_hypertension, cm_dyslipidemia, diabetes_any, prior_statin_use, has_prior_admission, med_vasopressor_24h, med_corticosteroid_24h, med_broad_abx_24h, med_insulin_24h; categorical race_group (ref White), insurance (ref Medicare), admission_type_grp (ref EW EMER.), first_careunit_grp (ref MICU), sepsis_category (ref sepsis). Log-transform lactate_max, creatinine_max, wbc_max, bun_max, glucose_max; log1p urine_output_24h_ml and hours_admit_to_icu (negative hours set to 0). Subgroups as in the published studies plus the design: age (<65, >=65), sex, sofa_tertile (SAPS II substitute), Charlson index (<3, >=3), septic shock (sepsis_category), organ_failure_any. Exclude post-baseline or outcome-defining variables and pf_ratio_min/sofa_respiration (~50% missing) from covariates.

In DuckDB SQL derive the covariates of the specification (female, diabetes_any, grouped categories, insurance 'Unknown', urine output < 0 set to missing, log transforms), the subgroup variables, and the outcomes: death_time_all = coalesce(deathtime, dod + 12 h); death28_all = death_time_all <= intime + 28 days, time28_all = days from intime to min(death_time_all, intime + 28 days) floored at 0; likewise death90_all/time90_all; hosp_death = hospital_expire_flag; icu_death = deathtime <= outtime + 6 h; icu_los_days = los; hosp_los_days = (dischtime - admittime) in days. Keep the design-specified outcome columns. No rows are dropped.

By exposure group and overall report n, 28-day and 90-day all-cause deaths with Wilson 95% CI, in-hospital and ICU deaths, median (IQR) ICU and hospital length of stay, design-specified in-hospital 28-day deaths, discharges alive before day 28, exposure timing (0-24 h vs 24-48 h) and deaths before 48 h.

Missing count and percentage per specified covariate overall and by exposure group; flag covariates above 40% missing as not imputable (published studies excluded variables above 20-50% missing; none of the specified covariates exceeds 20%).

Create m=20 imputations (20 iterations, seeds 20261120+k) of the continuous PS covariates on their transformed scale using chained Bayesian linear regression draws with exposure, death28_all, the Nelson-Aalen cumulative hazard at time28_all and all complete covariates as predictors; clip to the observed range; never impute exposure or outcomes. Save long format with an imputation index.

analysis_method: Unweighted baseline summary and standardized mean differences
operation: On observed data by exposure group: mean, SD, median, IQR and missing n for continuous covariates; n (%) for binary covariates and categorical levels; absolute SMD with pooled SD.

Within each imputation fit a multivariable logistic regression of pravastatin_exposed on all PS covariates; record convergence, separation and C-statistic; if any imputation fails to converge or separates, refit all imputations with L2-penalized logistic regression (C=1.0).
Per imputation and exposure group report PS minimum, 1/5/50/95/99th percentiles, maximum and the number outside the other group's range; save 20-bin histogram counts for imputation 1.

Within each imputation, as in the published MIMIC-IV statin-sepsis studies, match each pravastatin patient to one unexposed patient by greedy nearest-neighbour matching on the propensity score without replacement, processing exposed patients in descending PS order, with a caliper of 0.05 on the PS scale. Assign a pair_id to each matched pair, record unmatched exposed patients, and save the matched cohorts in long format.

Per imputation compute absolute SMDs of every covariate and categorical level in the matched cohort (pooled SD of the matched groups), average across imputations, classify balanced when the averaged SMD < 0.10, and report matched pairs and unmatched exposed patients per imputation.

Within each imputation compute stabilized ATE weights p/PS for exposed and (1-p)/(1-PS) for unexposed (sw_raw), truncate at the 1st and 99th percentiles within each exposure group (sw), and also compute overlap weights (1-PS for exposed, PS for unexposed).

Per imputation and exposure group summarize sw, sw_raw and overlap weights (mean, SD, percentiles, maximum, effective sample size) and compute weighted SMDs for each weighting, averaged across imputations, with the 0.10 balance criterion.

Build Table 1 in the format of the published studies: per covariate, pravastatin and no-pravastatin summaries and SMD in the full cohort, then in the matched cohort (imputation 1 values for counts; SMD averaged over imputations), plus the IPTW SMD.

analysis_method: Kaplan-Meier survival in the matched cohort
operation: Within each imputation's matched cohort estimate Kaplan-Meier survival to day 28 for the primary outcome by exposure group and the log-rank test; report survival on days 0-28 averaged over imputations, 28-day mortality by group and the median log-rank p-value; also report unmatched Kaplan-Meier curves.

analysis_method: Primary Cox regression in the matched cohort
operation: Within each imputation's matched cohort fit a Cox proportional-hazards model of time28_all/death28_all on pravastatin_exposed with robust variance clustered on pair_id (Efron ties), pool log hazard ratios across imputations with Rubin's rules, and report the HR, 95% CI and p-value.

Test the PH assumption for pravastatin_exposed in each imputation's primary matched Cox model with scaled Schoenfeld residuals (rank and log time) and report the median p-value; if it is below 0.05, report the 28-day risk difference and odds ratio from the matched cohort as the primary effect measure.

analysis_method: Multivariable Cox models in the full cohort
operation: As in the published studies, fit three Cox models of the primary outcome in the full cohort within each imputation and pool with Rubin's rules: Model 1 unadjusted; Model 2 adjusted for age, sex and race_group; Model 3 adjusted for all PS covariates.

analysis_method: Secondary outcomes in the matched cohort
operation: In each imputation's matched cohort: Cox model for 90-day all-cause mortality (pair-clustered robust variance); logistic regression with pair-clustered sandwich variance for in-hospital mortality and ICU mortality (odds ratios); all pooled by Rubin's rules. Report median (IQR) ICU and hospital length of stay by group with the Mann-Whitney test in the imputation 1 matched cohort.

In each imputation's matched cohort fit pair-clustered Cox models with pravastatin_exposed, subgroup indicators and their interactions for age (<65, >=65), sex, sofa_tertile, Charlson index (<3, >=3), septic shock and organ_failure_any; pool stratum HRs with Rubin's rules and the interaction with a pooled multivariate Wald test; report strata with fewer than 5 deaths in either group as not_estimable.

Pooled Cox HRs for the primary outcome with: (a) stabilized truncated IPTW (design-specified ATE), (b) untruncated stabilized IPTW, (c) overlap weights, (d) 1:1 PSM with caliper 0.2 SD of the logit PS, (e) complete-case PSM without imputation, (f) PSM restricted to no prior statin use and (g) to prior statin use, re-estimating the PS in each subset. Report n, deaths and balance (maximum SMD) for each.

(h) 48-hour landmark: restrict to patients alive at 48 h (time28_all > 2), restart follow-up at the landmark, re-impute, re-estimate the PS, 1:1 PSM (caliper 0.05) and pair-clustered Cox, pooled. (i) Time-dependent exposure: in the full cohort split each patient's follow-up at hours_to_first_pravastatin so exposure switches from 0 to 1 at initiation, fit a time-varying Cox model adjusted for all PS covariates in each imputation, and pool.

analysis_method: Design-specified in-hospital outcome and competing risks
operation: Using the design-specified outcome (followup_days, death_28d; patients discharged alive censored at discharge), fit the pair-clustered Cox model in the matched cohorts and a Fine-Gray model treating discharge alive (event_status 2) as the competing event (competing-event patients kept in the risk set to day 28 because the only censoring is administrative), with matched-cohort cumulative incidence of death at day 28; pool by Rubin's rules.

Combine the primary, multivariable, secondary-outcome, sensitivity, design-outcome and subgroup results into Table 2 (analysis, population, outcome, n and deaths by group, effect measure, estimate, 95% CI, p-value, status, note), and add the E-value for the primary HR and its confidence limit closest to 1 using RR = (1-0.5^sqrt(HR))/(1-0.5^sqrt(1/HR)). Keep not_estimable rows without invented values.
